shill: cellular: simplify service storage identifier construction This CL simplifies the service storage identifier construction code in Cellular::CreateService(): - A non-empty MobileOperatorInfo::uuid() implies MobileOperatorInfo::IsMobileNetworkOperatorKnown() is true, so redunduant MobileOperatorInfo::IsMobileNetworkOperatorKnown() checks are removed. - ICCID is absent on a CDMA only device without any SIM. shill: cellular: simplify service storage identifier initialization The storage identifier used by a CellularService object is supposed to settle on a value before the CellularService object is registered with the Manager. Currently, the storage identifier of a CellularService object is initialized in the CellularService constructor and then set again by the Cellular object before the CellularService object is registered with the Manager. This CL moves all the storage identifier initialization code to the CellularService constructor and removes CellularService::SetStorageIdentifier. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests. Change-Id: I9681012eac5e8c73705a9dc828640b3d59390661 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/737938 Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

shill: cellular: change service storage identitifer to use IMEI/MEID CL:404633 improved the cellular service profiling match to handle cellular devices with a randomly generated MAC address. However, the storage identifiers for cellular service are still constructed based on the MAC address. The chance of MAC address collision for two distinct cellular devices is non-zero. CL:715179 changed the storage identitifers for cellular device to leverage unique identitifers such as IMEI or MEID when available. This CL changes the storage identitifers for cellular service to use the same approach for consistency. Due to service profile matching logic introduced in CL:404633, changing the storage identitifers for cellular service won't break existing profiles. BUG=None TEST=Tested the following: - Run unit tests. - Manually verify that shill finds an older service profile based on the storage identifier that matches the MAC address of a modem. - Using a modem that is assigned a random MAC address by the kernel driver, manually verify that shill finds a matching service profile based on other service properties even when the storage identifier doesn't match the MAC address. - Verify that the storage identitifer of a newly created cellular service uses the IMEI of the cellular device instead of the MAC address. Change-Id: Id4642f8051a00b66d6894953808c6cf047955e71 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/737939 Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

[autotest] Fix constraints in hqe_by_insert_time get_host_queue_entries_by_insert_time was showing some strange behavior because it was making a wrong assumptions about the gap between insert-time and start-time being small. - Renamed to "get_host_queue_entries_by_start_time" - Changed the API to be based on started_on constraints. - Changed the function to infer only correct insert-time constraints. This means we cannot assume any lower bound on the insert-time, because the gap between insert and start times may be arbitrarily large. - Added more unit test coverage. BUG=chromium:748209 TEST=unit tests pass. Add udev rule: Limit the scheduler queue size for eMMC devices By default, the scheduler queue size - nr_requets - is set to 128. Given we are not supporing eMMC queueing feature, the IO device queue is 2, leaving 126 for merging. When the eMMC storage device is saturated with command, IO can be stuck up to 4 seconds in the queue. Instead, we should propagate the saturation and put the processes to sleep earlier. Limiting the queue size to 32 allow passing android.filesystem.cts.AlmostFullTest#testRandomRead more often. BUG=b:65528573 TEST=test_that --iterations=10 100.127.1.97 cheets_CTS_N.x86.CtsFileSystemTestCases passes 6/10 times instead of always failing on Caroline. Change-Id: I819385c197d5b9a94585ef59748fd4ad42c5ca1e Signed-off-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/738313
